metadata.title: Guideline 1 Application — AGENTS.md Authoring
metadata.author: Denis
metadata.purpose: Create the repository-level AGENTS.md context file for coding agents, following Topic-2 Guideline 1 (Context-Aware Grounding via Minimal Manual Documentation). Derive content from the binding SPEC and ADR; keep the file minimal, manually written, and non-redundant with existing docs.

conversation.content: Take @gse-project-impl/ as the context for the project. Based on Topic-2_Guidelines.md Guideline 1. create an AGENTS.md. From the context you will need to use design/ and specifications/ to produce the instructions file.

conversation.summary: Read Topic-2_Guidelines.md (Guideline 1 — Context-Aware Grounding via Minimal Manual Documentation), gse-project-impl/README.md, specifications/SPEC.md and SPEC_M1.md (v2.0 ambiguity-resolved baseline), and design/ADR.md (ADR-FINAL-P2: Hexagonal + Strategy/Command/Builder/Memento; DR-1..DR-7 drift risks). Authored gse-project-impl/AGENTS.md as a minimal, manually written context file.
design_decisions: Followed Guideline 1's 'good example' shape: no directory tree, no codebase overview, no architecture re-explanation — those live in ADR.md and SPEC_M1.md and the file just points at them.

Restricted content to non-obvious constraints an agent would silently get wrong by default: the Core.* import boundary, the no-literal-20/no-literal-4 rule (FR-1.2 / DR-1), Memento-as-source-of-truth on reload (DR-4), the lexicographic determinism contract (FR-3.4 / DR-3), and the procedural-Bootstrap rule (DR-7).
Listed both Java/Maven and Python/uv build commands per NFR-2.1 because the project had not yet committed to a language; flagged that the unused branch should be removed once chosen.
Pinned UML to v2 per design/README.md ('Use this version, not V1!') to prevent agents from regenerating against the stale diagram.
Explicitly excluded Milestone 2 (Duo) per ADR scope and DR-6.
Added a short 'When extending' section so new player adapters, rule changes, and config knobs land at the right hex layer instead of leaking into the core.

artifact.purpose: Repository-level context file consumed by coding agents (Claude Code, etc.) on every session.

conversation.content: The python is chosen now as the programming language for the project. Update everything to clearly state this.

conversation.summary: Updated AGENTS.md to commit to Python/uv and updated README.md to record the language choice. Deliberately did not retroactively edit SPEC_M1.md or ADR.md, since those are baseline / decision-record documents whose 'Java or Python' phrasing reflects NFR-2.1 as written — the language selection is a downstream commitment recorded in the live coding-agent context.
design_decisions: AGENTS.md: replaced the dual Java/Python build section with a Python-only 'Language & build / test / run' section, locking in uv as the package/env manager and rejecting pip/poetry/conda/setup.py workflows.

AGENTS.md: added a Python-specific mapping for the four hexagonal patterns — ports → typing.Protocol (or abc.ABC); value objects (ConfigVO, Memento, move Command) → @dataclass(frozen=True); Strategy → plain classes implementing the PlayerInput Protocol — so the architectural contract is concrete in the chosen language.
AGENTS.md: narrowed the no-GUI list to Python libraries (Tk, Qt, PyGame).
README.md: added a single-line 'Implementation language: Python (uv)' header pointing at AGENTS.md.
Left SPEC_M1.md and ADR.md untouched; flagged this trade-off to the user and offered an ADR addendum as the conventional alternative if a retroactive narrowing is desired.

artifacts.change: Replaced Java/Python dual build section with Python/uv-only commitment; added Python-specific pattern mapping; updated no-GUI library list.
Added 'Implementation language: Python (uv)' line referencing AGENTS.md.
